thread:
maya: Heads-up — seeing short bursts of apiserver p95/p99 latency in eu-west1 since ~02:10 UTC. controller-manager leader renewals show intermittent failures and a few pods entering ImagePullBackOff at the same time. Not sure if this is pure apiserver saturation or network/NAT churn.

luke: I picked up a stack of apiserver 5xx and watch reconnects. Also CPU spiking on the apiserver nodes during the bursts. Logs show a lot of `Get /api/v1/namespaces` fanout.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0420-01 — apiserver latency spike eu-west1. Pager duty notified.

maya: paste of `kubectl top pods -n kube-system` and short logs:
```
NAME                                     CPU(cores)   MEMORY(bytes)
kube-apiserver-eu-west-1a                 900m         1.2Gi
kube-apiserver-eu-west-1b                 1.1        1.3Gi
kube-controller-manager-eu-west-1a       120m         200Mi
```
and snippet: `E0420 02:10:34.123] apiserver watch: client disconnected: read tcp 10.0.5.3:6443: i/o timeout`

serena: Noticed NAT gateway SNAT ports exhausted earlier from image pulls during a rolling GPU node onboarding. That generated a lot of short connections to the registry -> lots of ephemeral ports. Could be correlation.

luke: +1 — I see a spike in conntrack `ESTABLISHED` counts on the proxy nodes around the same time. If SNAT saturated, new API requests could get queued/dropped which looks like apiserver latency from the controllers.

toni: Anyone check controller-manager leader lease events? If renewals missed, controllers will step down and try to reacquire which adds churn.

maya: `kubectl get events -n kube-system --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Lease` shows multiple leader transitions starting at 02:11.

ryan: Quick mitigation we did: increased SNAT pool size for the NAT gateway in eu-west1 and bumped iptables conntrack max on the proxies temporarily. That dropped the immediate 5xx rate.

serena: Actions we took and why:
- increased NAT ports on gateway to 2x (quick AWS rule change)
- rolled proxy nodes with tuned `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` and reduced conntrack timeout for TIME_WAIT to 30s for image pulls pattern
- scaled apiserver deployment from 3->5 replicas for the control-plane subnet (short term)

luke: Also patched kube-controller-manager to increase `--leader-elect-lease-duration` from 15s -> 45s in the canary pool to reduce churn while we stabilize networking. Note: this reduces failover speed but avoids repeated elections while connectivity flaps.

toni: Need to be careful with increasing apiserver replicas — we saw CPU decode pressure previously due to larger watch fanout. Any longer-term fix needs to reduce fanout (use informers/aggregators) and enable watch caching on high-traffic resources.

maya: Confirmed end-to-end that after the NAT and conntrack changes, p99 dropped back to baseline by ~02:28 UTC. Controller-manager leader elections stopped flapping.

ops-bot: Status update: INC-2026-0420-01 — mitigated at 02:28 UTC. Monitoring set to observe for 2h.

serena: Postmortem notes / follow-ups (short):
- runbook: add NAT capacity check into app rollout runbook for GPU node onboards (image pull storm can saturate SNAT)
- infra: consider regional image cache / ECR mirror near GPU pools to avoid registry egress spikes
- platform: add proactive conntrack/autoscale alert on proxy nodes (conntrack > 70% of limit)
- infra: evaluate managed NAT autoscaling vs fixed pool cost tradeoffs (estimate monthly delta vs outages)
- platform: add apiserver watch cache for CRDs with high-list frequencies and audit top-10 watchers per minute

luke: Also file a ticket to review default controller-manager leaseDuration semantics for our multi-AZ clusters. If leader flips are user-visible, maybe have a safer default for clusters with overloaded proxies.

toni: For immediate follow-up: schedule a focused test — spin up 50 GPU nodes in staging and run image-pull storm to validate SNAT and conntrack behavior. Capture metrics (SNAT usage, conntrack, apiserver p99, leader transitions).

maya: +1. I'll own the staging test and post steps in #eng-sre-playbooks.

ryan: FYI — cost note: doubling NAT pool and adding mirroring will add ~+$2.8k/month for eu-west1 based on current egress. Tagging finance for approval if we go managed autoscale route.

serena: Thanks team. We'll keep the incident open for the 2h observation window then close with postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:

luke: small add — add an alert that correlates controller-manager lease events with apiserver 5xx spikes so we can auto-surface this pattern next time.

maya: noted. closing actions in the incident tracker now.
